subject: Recap: reliability constraints, graceful-degradation options, and next steps (Catalyst Analytics)
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: ellen.park@catalyst-analytics.com, tbaker@catalyst-analytics.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-04-12T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: reliability constraints, graceful-degradation options, and next steps

Hi Ellen / Tom —

Thanks again for the 45-minute conversation earlier today. Below is a concise recap to make sure we captured pain, success criteria, and immediate next steps. If anything looks off, flag it and I’ll update.

Pain points we heard
- Recent regional incidents (Nov/Dec 2025) caused prolonged tail-latency spikes and two automatic retries in production; primary business impact: delayed transaction scoring and a small number of customer timeouts.
- Need predictable behavior during GPU saturation: current stack falls back to queueing which increases latency beyond acceptable limits.
- Compliance requirement: customer data must remain in-region for EU customers (affects routing rules).

Current stack (from convo)
- Ingest + feature pipeline on EKS (AWS) in us-east-1/us-west-2.
- Serving layer is a mix of internal microservices and an external tokenization/embedding vendor for search features.
- No dedicated reserved inference pool today; they run mixed workloads on shared GPU instances.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
- P99 inference latency <= 500 ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) under 95% load profile.
- Recovery from regional failure (route + warm fallback) < 2 minutes.
- Transparent cost profile: ability to estimate cost/unit for steady vs burst traffic.

Reliability / graceful-degradation options discussed
- Preferred: model-level fallback to a smaller quantized variant in the same region to maintain latency with degraded quality.
- Regional fallback: automatic routing to a secondary region (eu-west-1 or us-west-2) for non-EU traffic; EU traffic must remain in eu-west-1 per compliance.
- Cache and prefix reuse to reduce token churn on repeated API calls.

Immediate next steps (owners & timeline)
1) I’ll send a short recap + incident summary (attached) — ACTION: jonas_weber — today (attached).
2) Catalyst to confirm which customer segments must remain in-region for data residency — ACTION: ellen.park — by 2026-04-14.
3) We (Redwood) to run a quick fit assessment for: a reserved pool + fallback 7B quantized model cost estimate — ACTION: marissa_cole (pricing) & rishi_malhotra (infra) — by 2026-04-16.
4) Schedule a 30-min technical follow-up with engineering to validate routing and KV-cache assumptions — target week of 2026-04-19.

Attachments: 20260412-catalyst-recap.pdf (recap + notes), incident-summary-q4-2025.csv (extracted from your SLA logs)

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive once you confirm availability.

Best,

Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0132

Jonas — thanks, this is very helpful and captures the discussion broadly. A few clarifications: 

- Data residency: confirmed — our EU enterprise customers must have inference and token storage in eu-west-1. US customers can route to us-east-1 or us-west-2.
- Incident detail: we had two incidents in Q4 (11/03 and 12/18). The 11/03 issue was a degraded model cache which caused retries and approx ~45k affected requests; the 12/18 event was a regional networking blip with ~6-minute failover.
- For success criteria, add business impact to the latency goal: 500ms p99 should keep customer-facing latency below our SLA threshold (we’ll share the SLA doc before the deep-dive).

We’re available for the technical call on Tues 2026-04-20 between 10–12 PT. Please loop in your engineering lead for kernel/quantization questions.

Agree on the next steps; Tom and I will confirm the residency list by 2026-04-14.

Thanks,
Ellen
Director of Platform Engineering | Catalyst Analytics
ellen.park@catalyst-analytics.com

Subject: Proposed MAP & initial pricing estimate (Catalyst Analytics)

Ellen / Tom —

Appreciate the clear notes. Attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan and a back-of-envelope pricing estimate for the reserved pool + warmed 7B fallback (per region). Highlights:

- Reserved pool: baseline footprint sized to your steady-state request rate with ability to burst 2x for up to 10 minutes without queueing; monthly commit model available.
- Warmed 7B quantized fallback: designed to serve <10% of peak qps with degraded quality but stable latency; incremental monthly fee + minor per-token usage.
- SLA options: Dedicated (SLA-backed) vs Hosted + fallback. Dedicated lets us commit to 99.9% uptime and a p99 latency SLO; Hosted with fallback offers strong availability but requires the MAP for warm caches and cross-region replication to reach similar RTO targets.

Next steps we propose:
- You confirm residency segments and which customers need strict in-region processing by 2026-04-14 (Ellen).
- Technical deep-dive with our infra/serving lead (rishi.malhotra) on 2026-04-20 10:30 PT (we’ll send invite).
- We finalize MAP and a contract sketch (pricing + SLA options) by 2026-04-23.

Attachments: catalyst-mutual-action-plan-2026.xlsx (MAP), pricing-summary-catalyst.pdf

If that looks good I’ll send the calendar invite and a short doc that contrasts Dedicated vs Hosted fallback economics for your finance team.

Best,
Marissa Cole
